summary: The core is laid out as the physical board: a CPU board and a video board, with a separate module for each custom hybrid chip (N-8633-S timing generator, N-8633-V tilemap RAM, M67673 scroll adder, M67636 color blender), and signals named after the chips that drive them (DFFD_7E_A_Q, DFFQ_8F_Q2). Sprites are drawn by a Z80 BUSRQ DMA into a sprite table RAM, then by LS161-style counters stepped by a sequencer PROM into even/odd frame-buffer SRAMs. Blending is done by 4-bit adders with a carry and a force-white output, and grayscale comes from a LUT PROM. None of this follows MAME's draw_sprites loop, its tilemap callbacks, its (r+g+b)/3 grayscale, or jaleco_blend's clamped add/subtract.

findings.note: Each custom hybrid gets its own module, with chip-like ports (i_IOEN_n/i_IODIR LS245 direction, i_ENDOFTILELINE_n, o_TILEATTRSEL, o_CARRY). MAME has no such split: it uses generic tilemaps plus a jaleco_blend device.

findings.signal: board-net naming and discrete flops from raster bits
findings.note: Sync, blanking and interrupt timing come from separate flip-flop registers named after their chips (DFFD_7H_A/B, DFFD_8E_A/B, DFFD_7E_A/B, LS175 DFFQ_8F), all clocked from the H/V counter. These signals are carried across the CPU-board/video-board boundary as ports.

findings.where: rtl/Psychic5_cpuboard/Psychic5_obj.v: DMA SECTION, objdma_start_n/o_OBJDMA_BUSRQ_n; Psychic5_cpuboard.v:150-175 (T80 BUSRQ_n/BUSAK_n)
findings.note: Sprite RAM is copied into a private 6116 table RAM by stalling the CPU over BUSRQ, with address counters built like 5J/4J/4H LS161s with carry chaining. MAME just reads m_spriteram directly in a for loop.

The 32x32 sprite case comes from cascaded 4-bit counters whose carry routing changes with obj_size, and the PROM outputs drive the counter loads and next_objcode. MAME instead makes four explicit draw_sprite calls with x0/x1/y0/y1 offsets.

findings.signal: even/odd pixel frame buffer with board WE gating
findings.note: Two byte-wide SRAMs each hold one pixel of a pair. Write enables are NAND/AND products of offscreen, disable, transparency and init signals, writes are pulled up to FF when empty, and the read side is an output latch clocked by hcntr[0].

findings.signal: carry-based blender instead of clamped arithmetic
findings.note: Each channel is a 4-bit adder (tilemap + sprite + blendmode). Subtraction comes from an XOR'd input and a carry-in, and the carry output drives outen/forcewhite. MAME's func instead clamps 8-bit add/subtract to 0..255.
Grayscale is a 512x4 PROM lookup addressed by the top 3 bits of each palette channel, applied per pixel at output time. MAME recomputes the palette entries with an arithmetic average.

findings.signal: scan-time tile fetch with scroll adders
findings.where: rtl/Psychic5_videoboard/Psychic5_video.v: HSCROLL/VSCROLL M67673 instances, LS283 hscroll_msb_sum, tmbg_rom_addr, pixel latches
findings.note: Scroll registers are added to the flipped H/V counter bus every pixel, and the ROM nibble is selected through a 157-style mux. MAME uses per-frame tilemap scroll and TILE_GET_INFO callbacks.

findings.signal: decode as gate logic on bank bit
findings.note: Chip selects are expressions combining address bits, rambanknum and memspace_en_n (RFSH/MREQ), driving per-RAM CS lines. Write handlers are not used. The addresses themselves must match MAME either way.

Two interrupt flops are set by edges of the delayed 8F/8E timing signals and cleared asynchronously by M1&IORQ acknowledge. The vector is wired from DFFQ_8F_Q1_DLYD_n bits, whereas MAME's scanline timer callback picks fixed vectors by scanline number.
The F002/F003 bank registers, the C000-D7FF RAM layout and the C308-C30C scroll registers match MAME, as any correct implementation must.
